children: By Johann M Cherian

Strong mining gains led European shares higher on Thursday, with the benchmark just shy of hitting a record high, while technology shares lagged as investors weighed the implications of a Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections.
The pan-European STOXX 600 index
rose 0.7% to 661.99 points by 0905 GMT. All major regional benchmarks were also higher, led by a 1.7% gain in Spain's IBEX
Basic resources (.SXPP) rose 2%, boosted by ArcelorMittal's
5% gain after the world's second-largest steel maker topped core profit expectations.
Investors were broadly relieved by a Democratic win in both houses of Congress in the US and that President Donald Trump acknowledged defeat.

Further, expectations were high that efforts to end the Iran conflict could be accelerated, while the Democrats could keep a check on excessive fiscal spending and policies targeting sectors such as European banks and clean energy.

However, uncertainty prevailed over the outlook for the global technology sector on concerns that increased scrutiny over data centre buildout could slow down spending on developing AI, although analysts highlighted that existing orders are unlikely to be affected.

"Concerns about a potential tightening of artificial intelligence regulations have not disappeared, but they appear to be offset for now by robust investment in data centers and resilient corporate earnings," said John Plassard, head of investment strategy at Cité Gestion, in a note.
Chip stocks including Siltronic
shed 7.3%, while chip equipment maker ASML
lost 2.4% and Soitec
was off 4.8%.
Asian tech stocks witnessed steep declines and US Nasdaq futures
shed 0.7%.
France's Legrand
gained 5.5% after raising its 2026 sales growth forecast for the second time this year on robust data centre demand.
Software stocks, which have had the overhang of AI disruption concerns this year, were also marginally higher. SAP
and Dassault Systemes
were up over 1% each.
Thursday also brought a wave of corporate earnings.
Rheinmetall
slid 16.5% after cutting its 2026 sales forecast for the second time in three months. Renewables such as Orsted
and Nordex
rose 4.2% and 4%, respectively, after they reported strong results.
Air France-KLM
gained over 11% after exceeding third-quarter operating profit expectations.
Aker BP
shed 11.2% after the UK's BP
said it sold a 5% stake in the Norwegian oil and gas company.
Later in the day, investors will be keen on interest rate decisions out of the UK.
